name: xLean TR1
description: Marketed by xLean Robotics as "the world's first dual-form transformable floor washing robot" — it switches between an autonomous robot vacuum/mop and a handheld stick vacuum in about a second. Crowdfunded on Kickstarter in 2026 before reaching preorder.

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: ~6.5 kg in robot mode; handheld mode is 2.02 lb (~0.9 kg) — official xLean spec

specs.label: Dimensions
specs.note: robot mode, radar up (13cm tall when retracted); official xLean spec

specs.label: Subscription
specs.note: No subscription mentioned in xLean's Kickstarter FAQ or site, but the app hasn't been reviewed in depth — product is still preorder/early-tester stage as of Sept 2026

sourcing: Specs sourced from xLean Robotics' own site (xlean.ai), its Kickstarter campaign page, and TechRadar's January 2026 hands-on coverage, as of September 2026. Battery life, dustbin capacity, and a firm retail price are not published by xLean and were not found in press coverage checked — these are omitted rather than estimated. As a crowdfunded, still-shipping-to-early-testers product, real-world performance and final specs may differ from what's advertised. robotindex does not sell this product.

pricing.summary: No confirmed retail price from any source checked. xLean's Kickstarter campaign (April 21–June 20, 2026) raised **$2,112,838** from 2,019 backers against a $100,000 goal; its early-tester program used a refundable **$50** deposit rather than a full purchase price. The official site currently offers preorders with a "Free Shipping Now" promotion but no listed dollar amount in the sources checked — treat any specific price seen elsewhere as unverified until confirmed on xlean.ai directly.

editorial.heading: Sensors & Hardware
editorial.body: The TR1 switches between autonomous robot mode and manual handheld mode: a retractable LiDAR puck detaches so a wand attachment can be added, while the same roller-mop-and-vacuum system works in both. Autonomous navigation uses 360° LiDAR, an RGB-D camera, and an AI chip, with carpet detection and recognition of 400+ object types. Battery life and dustbin capacity are undisclosed.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: xLean's Kickstarter campaign for the TR1 raised $2,112,838 from 2,019 backers against a $100,000 goal — a real, verified crowdfunding milestone, not a marketing claim. As a still-shipping, early-tester-stage product, battery life, dustbin capacity, and a firm retail price remain undisclosed.

firmwareCommunity.note: xLean TR1 has not released a public SDK, firmware repo, or developer API. Not currently listed in Builds & Mods.
